hook: Danijar Hafner is a machine learning researcher known for developing the Dreamer family of world-model algorithms for reinforcement learning. He completed a Master of Research at University College London and the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, mentored by Timothy Lillicrap and Karl Friston, then earned his PhD at the University of Toronto advised by Jimmy Ba as a Vanier Scholar. During this time he was also a visiting student at UC Berkeley under Pieter Abbeel and completed a multi-year internship at Google Brain. He created PlaNet and the original Dreamer algorithm, which learns behaviors by imagining future outcomes inside a learned latent world model, then led development of DreamerV2 and DreamerV3. He is now a Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind, where he continues to work on world models, temporal abstraction, and scalable self-improvement for AI agents.
name: Danijar Hafner

quote.text: Building generally intelligent machines that understand and interact with the world
quote.context: Research philosophy statement on his personal website, danijar.com

moniker: World model researcher, creator of the Dreamer algorithms

timeline.event: Published Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination, the original Dreamer paper
timeline.impact: Showed that agents could learn effective behaviors purely by imagining trajectories inside a learned world model.

timeline.event: Published DreamerV2, Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models
timeline.impact: Became the first world-model-based agent to reach human-level performance on the Atari benchmark.

timeline.event: Published DreamerV3, Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
timeline.impact: Extended world-model reinforcement learning across dozens of domains with a single fixed set of hyperparameters.

timeline.event: Joined Google DeepMind as a Staff Research Scientist
timeline.impact: Continued world-model and self-improvement research at industrial scale.

quick_facts: Completed an MRes at UCL and the Gatsby Unit, mentored by Timothy Lillicrap and Karl Friston
Earned his PhD at the University of Toronto, advised by Jimmy Ba, as a Vanier Scholar
Created PlaNet and the Dreamer world-model algorithms, including DreamerV2 and DreamerV3
Also created Plan2Explore, LEXA, and the hierarchical planning algorithm Director
Was a visiting student at UC Berkeley under Pieter Abbeel and interned for several years at Google Brain
Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind

achievements.title: Created the Dreamer algorithm
achievements.impact: Introduced learning behaviors by imagining future outcomes inside a compact latent world model, a widely adopted approach to sample-efficient reinforcement learning.

achievements.title: DreamerV2 reached human-level Atari performance
achievements.impact: Showed that a world-model-based agent could match model-free reinforcement learning on a standard benchmark.

achievements.title: DreamerV3
achievements.impact: Delivered a single world-model algorithm that works across dozens of domains without per-task tuning.

achievements.title: Vanier Canada Graduate Scholar
achievements.impact: One of Canada's top graduate research honors, awarded for his PhD work at the University of Toronto.
